sonnet.problem: The card says 'there's that line again' about 'bloodshed against men and violence against the land, the city and all their dwellers.' Verse 8 reads 'bloodshed against man,' while verse 17 reads 'men,' so the lines are not an exact match. The earlier card (stop 1 card 7) also only paraphrased verse 8 ('He spilled blood and brought violence…'), so the baker was never shown these words.
sonnet.rule: Noticing: What he points out must be true. "Same words" means an exact match. He only points back to words a card has shown.

sonnet.problem: The question opens with 'This man places his nest up high.' It points back to a man named only on the previous card, which is no longer on screen, so the question never says who he is or what he did.
sonnet.rule: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.
